title: Chicken or Turkey Salad with Light Mayonnaise

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey salad mixed with light mayonnaise is a light dish popular in colder seasons. The poultry provides high‑quality protein, while the light mayo adds a gentle flavor with fewer calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
Light mayonnaise typically contains less fat and fewer calories than regular mayo, using reduced‑fat dairy or plant oils.
The salad is often served as an appetizer at festive tables and in children’s menus.
Traditional recipes include fresh vegetables such as cucumber, tomato, and herbs, boosting the vitamin content.
When stored properly, the salad stays fresh for up to 3‑4 days in the refrigerator.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Using light mayonnaise reduces the overall calorie and fat content compared with the classic version.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is abundant in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The salad provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and a modest amount of fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored chicken/turkey can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Light mayonnaise often contains egg yolk, which may trigger reactions in egg‑allergic individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some commercial light mayonnaises are high in salt; people monitoring sodium should watch portion size.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: The salad loses freshness quickly; after 3‑4 days it may develop off‑odors and should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, in sandwiches, on lettuce leaves, or as a side to soups. Add fresh veggies, herbs, nuts, or dried fruit for extra texture and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Consume within 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops a sour smell or discoloration.
